summary.name: Reqable
summary.one_liner: Reqable is a cross-platform API debugging proxy and REST client that combines HTTP(S) traffic capture with API testing, on desktop and mobile.
use_cases: Capturing and inspecting HTTP/HTTPS traffic from desktop apps
Debugging mobile app network requests without a Wi-Fi proxy
Testing REST APIs with headers, bodies and authorization
Rewriting or breaking requests to simulate test scenarios
Comparing request and response differences to locate bugs
Generating code snippets or cURL commands from requests
summary.what_it_does: Reqable runs a MITM debugging proxy on one port that accepts HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS4/4a and SOCKS5, with HTTP/2, WebSocket, gRPC and SSE traffic support. It lets users filter captured traffic by application, domain, data type and bookmarks, and build requests from traffic, cURL or collections. Users can define rewrite (map remote/map local) and breakpoint rules or write Python scripts to modify requests and responses. The REST client side supports editing parameters, headers, bodies, authorization, environment variables, cookies and importing Postman or Hoppscotch collections. Mobile traffic can be forwarded automatically to the desktop app.
notable: Combines a Fiddler/Charles-style debugging proxy with a Postman-style REST client
Desktop-to-mobile traffic forwarding without Wi-Fi proxy setup
Python scripting for request and response processing
Lightweight install of about 30M, with claimed fast startup and low memory use
caveats: Free community edition exists; a paid Professional Edition is promoted for continued development
Benchmark claims are from the vendor on an M5 MacBook Pro
